key_insight: A learned surrogate for 1-D arterial blood-flow models enables real-time, patient-specific hemodynamic predictions—preserving fidelity to physics-based simulations while reducing compute by orders of magnitude.
problem_solved: Addresses the high computational cost and clinical impracticality of running 1-D hemodynamic simulations at scale and the difficulty of estimating hard-to-measure terminal parameters (resistance/compliance) for personalized analysis.
method: Generate a wide-ranging dataset of 1-D arterial network simulations spanning physiologic variability and parameter uncertainty.
Train a fast surrogate emulator (e.g., neural-network or reduced-order model, optionally physics-informed) to map inputs (anatomy, boundary conditions, terminal R/C) to pressure/flow waveforms.

Personalize by inverting the surrogate (optimization or Bayesian inference) to estimate patient-specific terminal parameters and produce real-time hemodynamic predictions with uncertainty quantification.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a practical template for replacing expensive physics simulators with accurate, real-time surrogates—enabling large-scale cohort generation, closed-loop personalization, and deployment in clinical decision-support or digital-twin applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: clinical inputs → surrogate model → real-time pressure/flow outputs and parameter estimates
Runtime vs. accuracy chart: surrogate (ms) vs. full 1-D solver (s–min) with error bars
Example waveforms: measured vs. surrogate-predicted pressure and flow with uncertainty bands
Parameter-estimation heatmap: inferred terminal resistance/compliance across a cohort or anatomical map
paper_title: Real-Time Surrogate Modeling for Personalized Blood Flow Prediction and Hemodynamic Analysis
paper_authors: Sokratis J. Anagnostopoulos, George Rovas, Vasiliki Bikia, Theodore G. Papaioannou, Athanase D. Protogerou
